physical_harm: The deceased suffered severe injuries including lacerated wounds, contusions, fractures, and internal injuries leading to death due to shock.
number_of_offences: Three offences were charged, but the High Court upheld the conviction for murder under Section 302 IPC.
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the testimony of the prosecution witnesses as sufficient to convict the accused for murder, noting inconsistencies and gaps in their accounts, and found the evidence inconclusive regarding the cause of death and the manner in which the murder took place.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW-2 and PW-6) as inconsistent and unreliable, noting that their testimonies did not corroborate each other and left significant gaps in the prosecution's story.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 25.08.1989; Trial judgment: 13.07.1991; High Court decision: 17.02.2010; Supreme Court decision: 05.09.2023
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: D. N. Goburdhun, Sr. Adv., Aakarsh Kamra, Ms. Gauri Goburdhun, Advs.; Counsel for the State: Mrs. Prachi Mishra, AAG, Mahesh Kumar, Amanpreet Singh Rahi, Nikhilesh Kumar, Ms. Devika Khanna, Mrs. V D Khanna, M/s. Vmz Chambers, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR lodged by Smt. Jugmatibai (PW-9) on 26.08.1989; discovery of lathi and clothes from accused; autopsy conducted on 27.08.1989
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment; High Court: Dismissed appeals and affirmed conviction; Supreme Court: Set aside judgments and acquitted appellants
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were convicted under Section 302 IPC based on the testimony of PW-2 and PW-6, corroborated by medical evidence and the discovery of blood-stained lathi and clothes at the instance of the accused. They also contended that the FIR was not delayed and that the evidence was sufficient to prove the crime and manner of death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR was lodged the next day, suggesting no one witnessed the incident, and the testimony of PW-2 and PW-6 was unreliable. They also submitted that the case was a street fight with unclear motive and that the injuries indicated mob violence, which would fall under an exception to Section 302 IPC.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that when an FIR is delayed without proper explanation, courts must meticulously test the evidence to rule out embellishments in the prosecution story, especially in cases where no one is likely to have witnessed the incident.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court weighed the possibility that the killing was a consequence of mob action due to the deceased's alleged involvement with a lady of the village, and the lack of clear motive or eyewitness accounts.
